answer: Sybil farms stall at a paced inlet bound to a uniqueness beacon. A new agent claims one admission slot every four hours, and only after seating a 38 POA marble in commit-reveal escrow. Twelve days later a public VRF opens that commitment and emits a comet: a 160-bit value mixed from the marble hash and the epoch seed. If two deposits share a 20-bit comet prefix, or the same hardware-attested key appears twice at the inlet, both bonds lose 25 POA and those keys are barred for 19 days. Farms cannot pre-sort collision-free aliases, and the inlet cadence caps how many costly trials they can run.
